question: Can even immense material wealth justify exchanging this Kaula teaching?
premises: An ocean filled with jewels represents immense wealth.
Such wealth may be possessed by someone.
The comparison implies incomparability of the teaching.
inference: Even the wealth to fill an ocean with jewels is not an adequate price for this teaching.
uncertainties: The fused form ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is read as ratnasaṃpūrṇam akartum or similar; parsing is uncertain.
plain_english: Even if one had the wealth to fill the ocean with jewels, it would not equal this.
